tabs.label: Spirit Commands
tabs.intro: SP costs come from the game data (cost table at ROM 0x100AD0, ordered by Spirit Command ID), and each effect is verified in code: a command can be cast as long as SP is at least the cost; “until next turn” means it's cleared for everyone when the next turn begins, so an effect used in the player phase lasts through the whole enemy phase. Compared with Akurasu, the descriptions of Trust, Faith, Resupply, Accel, Valor/Soul, Cover and Taunt differ, and many conditions Akurasu doesn't list are added.

blocks.title: Spirit Command list
rows: Destroys yourself, dealing damage equal to your current HP to every unit adjacent up, down, left or right (including allies), ignoring armor, terrain and barriers; units in Stealth take no damage, Libra takes only 10; unusable with no adjacent units {+}
View the target's status; usable only on enemies you have not yet fought or used Scan on, and the status stays visible afterward {+}
Move +3; kept as long as you don't move, not cleared at turn change
If the target has 20 HP or more and your Skill is strictly higher than theirs, the attack won't destroy them, leaving 10 HP; also works on counterattacks {+}
Completely evades one enemy attack; Flash takes priority when it meets Bullseye; stays until you're attacked, even across turns
Restores 30% of own max HP (rounded down); can't be used at full HP
100% hit rate, ignoring the target's Afterimage and Parry; if the target used Flash, Flash takes priority; Dummy can still block it {+}
Restores 30% of the chosen unit's max HP (rounded down) {≠}
Doubles own armor (doubled armor goes into the damage formula) {+}

The next time the chosen ally is attacked, you fight in its place, at any range; does not cover an ally that used Flash; ends if you are shot down or either unit boards, combines or uses Separate; no turn limit

Makes the chosen enemy target only you, at any range; it lasts until you are shot down, or either side boards, combines or Separates, with no turn limit; some bosses and elites are immune to Taunt {+}
Damage ×2 in the next battle (counterattacks included); can't be used while Valor or Soul is active
All pilots of the unit get Will +10 (max 150)
Fully restores own HP; unusable at full HP
Funds ×2 from the next battle (multiplied with the kill bonus; at most 65,535 per unit destroyed)
Target enemy unit's pilots all get Will −10, down to a minimum of 50; the target's main pilot must have Will 51 or higher {+}
Damage ×3 in the next battle (counterattacks included); doesn't stack with Valor — an active Valor is cancelled on use (the SP spent on Valor is wasted) {+}
Can't be attacked by enemies, and targets can't counter its attacks; self-destructs can't hurt it either {+}
+1 action remaining this turn; used before acting, you can act twice this turn
Fully restores the target unit's EN and all ammo, at any range; Will is unchanged {≠}
Target unit's pilots all get Will +10 (max 150)
Halves the hit rate of every enemy on the map (third parties included), on counterattacks too; Bullseye and Flash are unaffected
All ally units on the map with HP not full (including self) recover 50% of max HP
All ally units on the map (including self) fully recover HP
Lets 1 unit that has already acted this turn act again
The in-game description is “????”; it actually triggers Guts, Spirit ×3, Accel, Bullseye, Flash, Soul and Fortune in turn, skipping any already active; costs only 100 SP
Each pilot on the target unit recovers 50 SP (up to the maximum)
Choose 1 destroyed ally unit to Revive beside you: HP, EN, ammo and SP fully restored, Will back to 100 (+5 per equipped Shuffle Crest), spirit effects cleared, and it can act this turn {+}
notes: “Duration” follows when the code clears the effect: Accel clears after the next move; Focus, Wall, Bullseye, Disrupt and Stealth clear for everyone when the turn count increases (the next turn); Valor, Soul, Fortune, Gain and Mercy clear after one battle ends, for both attacker and defender; Flash and Cover clear after triggering; Taunt lasts until a cancel condition occurs
Status-type Spirit Commands are recorded on the unit's main pilot, and ones used by sub-pilots also apply to the whole unit; the three pilots of a Getter-type unit share one set of statuses {+}
When a Spirit Command changes Will, it is capped at 150 and floored at 50 {+}

Points where Akurasu disagrees with the code: Trust (Akurasu: restores 2000), Faith (Akurasu: restores half HP to one ally), Resupply (Akurasu: target's Will −10; the Will drop actually comes from the unit command “Resupply” — the Spirit Command Resupply doesn't lower it), Accel (Akurasu: lasts 1 turn), Valor/Soul (Akurasu: one attack), Cover and Taunt (Akurasu: one battle) {≠}
The enemy AI never uses Spirit Commands on its own; any Spirit Command effects on enemies come from story commands and cost no SP {+}
The game data also has an unnamed Spirit Command no. 31 that nobody can learn: cost 1, own Will +30; never used in normal play {+}

blocks.title: Details verified in code
items: Flash takes priority over Bullseye: the hit check first looks at whether the defender has Flash — if so, it's 0% outright — and only then at the attacker's Bullseye

Bullseye sets hit rate straight to 100%, unaffected even by the halving when the defender picks the “Evasion” command; it also skips the Afterimage and Parry checks, but Dummy, barriers such as Aura Barrier and I-Field, and Shield still apply {+}{≠}
Focus is symmetric: +30 hit when attacking, −30 to the attacker's hit when attacked
Disrupt marks every enemy; marked enemies have their hit rate halved when attacking and countering, stacking with the halving from the “Evasion” command (down to 1/4 at most)
Wall counts the defender's armor at 2× in the damage formula; it doesn't halve damage
Soul (×3) and Valor (×2) don't stack; with both active Soul applies; no criticals while either is active
Mercy compares both sides' Skill and requires yours to be strictly higher; it has no effect if the target has under 20 HP, so the target may be shot down {+}
HP restored is max HP × the rate, fractions dropped
The hit roll is 1–99, so 99% and 100% hit rates have the same effect in practice

tabs.label: Pilot skills
tabs.intro: All skill values come from ROM tables and battle code. In the original, several skills' code does not match their descriptions; this port's “Gameplay adjustments” turn these fixes on by default, and you can switch each one off on the “Rules” page of the settings to restore original behavior.

blocks.title: Skill effects: original and this port
rows: Hit and evasion rise with level; can use NT-only weapons; Funnel-type range increases

Hit and evasion at L1–L9: +10, 14, 18, 21, 24, 26, 28, 29, 30; Funnel, Fin Funnels, Mother Funnel and Reflector Bit need L1 to use, the MAP versions need L4; at L7 and L8 the 11 Funnel-type weapons get +1 max range, at L9 +2; Reflector Bit gets no range bonus {+}{+}
Raises evade and Aura Barrier; L1 enables Aura Slash, L3 enables Hyper Aura Slash and other weapons

Regardless of level, always −32 to the enemy's hit when attacked (even at skill level 0, before it shows on the status page); no modifier when attacking; Hyper Aura weapons get no power bonus; the Aura Barrier threshold rises with level (see “Unit Status”)

Evasion by level: L1 +10 … L9 +30 (same curve as NT); the power of Hyper Aura Slash, Hyper Aura Cannon, Hyper Aura Shot Arm and Twin Aura Attack gets a level bonus: L3 +600, L4 +800, L5 +1000, L6 +1200, L7 +1300, L8 +1400, L9 +1500 (the normal Aura Slash doesn't)
Raises hit and evade (the description also mentions attack power)
Regardless of level: +64 hit when attacking, −64 to the enemy's hit when attacked; the attack power bonus doesn't exist at all in the original code
Hit and evasion by level: L1 +10 … L9 +30; the attack power bonus is still not implemented
The lower the HP, the higher the hit, evasion and critical rates
All bands shift one step earlier: there is already a bonus at 90%+ HP (L9 +10), and the top band is reached below 20% HP; hit, evade and critical get the same value, up to +90 at L9
No bonus at full HP (90%+); the top band only below 10% HP; hit and evade bonuses are halved (up to +45 at L9), critical unchanged (up to +90)
When the unit carries a sword-type weapon, blocks an attack completely by chance

Player side level÷16 (actually 57% at L9), enemy side level÷32 (actually 29% at L9); works only on weapons marked “parryable”: Missile, Torpedo, grenades and other solid-ammo weapons, plus about two thirds of Melee weapons; Beam weapons, vulcan-type shooting, and some Melee finishers such as Sekiha Tenkyoken and Burning Finger cannot be parried; does not trigger when the attacker uses Bullseye {≠}
When the unit carries a shield, halves damage by chance

Chance is the same as Parry (player ÷16, enemy ÷32, regardless of the incoming weapon); halved damage is rounded down to a multiple of 10, minimum 10; does not trigger on damage under 20; Bullseye cannot bypass it; not checked once Aura Barrier is broken through {≠}
At Will 130 or higher, activates automatically when the specified pilot is in the specified Gundam

Domon, Argo, Sai Saici, George, Chibodee (only while on your side) and Master Asia, each in his own Gundam, switch to S/H mode at Will ≥130: max HP / EN +200/+50 (current values rise proportionally), mobility +10, limit +10, unit and weapon land, sea and space ratings become A (air unchanged), all pilot stats +10 and all pilot terrain ratings A, and their signature finishers gain attack power by pilot level (see the table below); the Burning Gundam H also gains God Shadow. An enemy Allenby in the Noble Gundam goes into Berserker mode, with only the unit bonuses. Once triggered it isn't cancelled by Will dropping — only when the unit is shot down {≠}{+}{+}{+}
Gained when the pilot reaches the level set for each (see the pilot table below); the unit info on the map shows W while two actions remain this turn
The more kills your pilot has, the more funds you get for destroying enemies

20–39 kills ×1.1, then +0.1 per 20 kills, ×2.0 from 200 kills; then multiplied with Fortune (up to ×4); at most 65,535 per unit destroyed; enemies don't get this bonus; experience isn't affected by kill count {≠}{+}

Battle calculation never reads Limit at all: on the status screen an excess only changes color, and Limit upgrades, Limit-raising parts, and the Limit boosts from V-MAX and Super Mode have no effect in battle

The attacker's “hit + Mobility” and the defender's “evade + Mobility” are each capped at their unit's Limit; a high-level pilot in a low-grade unit loses noticeable hit and evade, which is what makes Limit upgrades and parts worthwhile
notes: Both sides use the same rules: enemy ESP, Holy Warrior and Potential pilots are also calculated by this port's defaults
Critical rate = attacker's Skill − defender's Skill + weapon critical modifier, at least 1%; enemy attacks are further ÷4 and get no Potential bonus, so enemies almost never land criticals
Potential “halving” is backed only by community sources and unused data, weaker evidence than the other items; it can be turned off on its own if you don't like it

How skill level works: each pilot skill has 9 learn levels, and the skill level equals how many of them the pilot's current level has reached; NT, Enhanced, Holy Warrior, ESP and Potential share one level
EXP = (enemy pilot base EXP + enemy unit EXP) × level-difference factor (×3.4 when the enemy is 8+ levels higher, ×0.01 when 6+ levels lower); ÷10 without a kill, minimum 1; Gain ×2 {+}

blocks.title: How to switch Gameplay adjustments on and off
items: Open the settings in game and go to the “Rules” page: the “Corrections” group is on by default, the “Difficulty” group off by default
There are three presets: Restore defaults (corrections on, difficulty off), All off (original rules), All on
Changes take effect immediately, applying from the next battle resolution; the save format is unchanged, so you can switch rules on existing progress
7 fixes in total: ESP, Holy Warrior evasion, Limit, Potential tiers, Potential halving, swap weapon carry-over, Hyper Aura Slash power
There are 5 Difficulty options: boss dummies halved, boss dummies none, upgrade cap, departure refund, parts carry over

tabs.label: Unit Status
tabs.intro: Barrier abilities work very differently: Aura Barrier is “nothing unless pierced,” the I-Field types are “flat reduction, stackable,” and all of them work only against Beam shooting weapons and cost EN. Values and units come from ROM and battle code; the units listed after “Enemy” appear only on the enemy side.

blocks.title: Aura Barrier threshold
notes: The strategy guide prints +200…+1000, but the game actually uses this table; this port keeps the original values
The threshold doubles when the defender picks “Defense”; based on the main pilot's Holy Warrior level, 3000 without Holy Warrior {+}

blocks.title: Check order after a hit
items: Each attack first rolls to hit; only attacks that would hit go through these checks in order: Afterimage-type → Parry → Dummy → Barrier → Shield, stopping as soon as any one succeeds
So the Afterimage and Parry chances shown on screen are conditional probabilities “given a hit”
When the attacker uses Bullseye, Afterimage and Parry are skipped; Dummy, barriers and Shield are checked as usual {≠}
Barriers are checked only when the attacker uses a Beam shooting weapon and the defender has enough EN; once Aura Barrier is broken through, the I-Field types and Shield are no longer checked {+}
Damage is 0 when fully blocked by a barrier; otherwise minimum damage is 10

blocks.title: Dummy (enemy bosses only)
items: Some bosses have a number of Dummies: an attack that should hit is taken by the Dummy instead, the attack has no effect, and the count drops by 1; no roll, always works
Dummy is not used up when an attack is evaded or stopped by Afterimage or Parry; Dummy blocks attacks even when the attacker uses Bullseye {≠}
The game doesn't show the remaining count, and it doesn't recover between turns
In the original there are 42 deployment records with Dummy, all belonging to Haman, Char, Scirocco, Glemy, Milliardo, Gyunei, Gato and Le Cain, with 2, 3, 5 or 7 uses depending on the stage

Difficulty “Boss dummies: halved” changes 2/3/5/7 to 1/1/2/3; “Boss dummies: none” sets them to zero, and with both checked “none” wins; both off by default, and the new rule applies the next time a unit spawns
In the original, when Wufei appears as an enemy, his kill count from your side is used as his Dummy count; this port fixes that unconditionally, and he no longer has Dummy

tabs.label: Parts
tabs.intro: Part effects are from ROM and code analysis: when abilities are recalculated, each equipped part adds its bonus, matching the bonus table on the intermission screen and the in-game descriptions. Note that the original's “Limit” takes no part in battle calculation; only with this port's Limit correction on by default do Limit-raising parts actually do anything.

blocks.title: Parts on unit swaps
items: In the original, a swap (including the stage where the new unit is auto-deployed right after) returns all of the old unit's parts to storage; the parts aren't lost, they just can't be re-equipped until the next intermission
Difficulty “Parts carry over” (off by default): on a unit swap, the old unit's parts go straight onto the new unit in their original order, and any that don't fit go to storage
The five Customs (Wing Zero, Sandrock, Deathscythe Hell, Heavyarms, Altron) and Shin Getter have only 1 part slot, while the previous units had 2, so each of these changes leaves one part in storage
Before and after the transformation Dancouga is the same unit upgraded in place; the original also removes its parts

tabs.label: Love bonus
tabs.intro: Pairings come from the Love bonus table in ROM, with activation conditions from battle-code analysis. A pilot with the bonus deals +30% damage and takes −30% damage while the partner is within 2 squares (horizontal, vertical or diagonal, at most one square between).

blocks.title: Rules
items: Holder attacking → damage +30%; holder being attacked → damage taken −30%; hit rate unaffected
With multiple partners the bonus does not stack; at most ±30%
Effective only for ally pilots; the partner must also be an ally unit on the map
The partner must be within 2 squares of the holder: horizontal plus vertical distance of 2 or less (diagonally adjacent counts); it does not need to be on the current screen {?}
The bonus applies after damage is calculated, before the Valor / Soul / critical multipliers

tabs.label: Upgrades and inheritance
tabs.intro: SRW64's upgrade cap depends on the unit (6–15 levels): strong units get fewer, weak and mass-production units more. The increase and price of each level are the same for every unit and depend only on which level you're at. Values on this page come from the ROM's upgrade increment table, price table and unit data, recomputed cell by cell against the code; swap carry-over and story-granted levels come from parsing the carry-over table and the scripts.

tabs.label: Extra weapons

Unlock tables, weapon values and use conditions all come from ROM and code analysis; story unlock timing comes from script analysis.

notes: The unlock table comes from game data (the upgrade screen's full-upgrade unlock table, 18 entries): when a weapon's level exactly reaches the unit's upgrade cap, the corresponding weapon on the same unit unlocks. “Full upgrade cost” = cost per level × (1 + 2 + … + unit upgrade cap), with the per-level cost by weapon upgrade type: 5,000 for type 1, 4,000 for type 2

Five differences from Akurasu: Jagd Doga (120,000), MP Great Mazinger (300,000), Twin Buster Rifle MAP (110,000) and Gundam Heavyarms Kai (88,000) can't be reproduced with any type or cap; the Minerva X's 525,000 corresponds to treating cap 15 as 14 {≠}

“Friendly fire”: each MAP weapon has an ally-recognition flag, and flagged ones remove squares with allies on them from the area. In the whole game only Funnel MAP, Fin Funnels MAP, Splash Breaker MAP, Spiral Sword MAP and Mandala Circle Nirvana have this flag; all other MAP weapons hit every unit within range {+}

MAP ranges (facing up): Breast Fire / Breast Burn MAP is a 12-square fan within 4 squares ahead; Full Barrage MAP is 7 squares within 3 ahead; Go Flasher MAP is a 35-square fan within 5 ahead; Diffuse Bazooka MAP is a 9-square fan 3–5 squares ahead; Funnel MAP picks a center square within range 1–4 and hits a radius-2 diamond (13 squares), Fin Funnels MAP radius 3 (25 squares) {+}

tabs.label: Combination attacks
tabs.intro: Participation conditions, multipliers and values all come from the ROM's combination attack data and check code. A combination attack appears in the weapon list only when every participant meets its Will and EN requirements and they are connected on the map (diagonal adjacency counts; with three or more units, the group just needs to be connected as a whole, not every pair adjacent), and any participant can launch it. Attack power = the average of the current attack power (including upgrades) of each participating unit's corresponding component attack × multiplier, rounded down. Each participant pays the combination attack's EN once; no ammo is used.

tabs.label: GB link
tabs.intro: The original needs the 64GB Pak connected to the GB game Super Robot Wars Link Battler for F91, GoShogun and Zambot 3 to join. This port needs no cartridge: just check the series on the intermission screen. Unlock conditions, link stages and join levels all come from analysis of the ROM, scripts and code.

blocks.title: Recruitable series
rows: Have an F91-series unit, or have Seabook / Cecily
Have the GoShogun, or have Shingo
Zambot 3 (can Separate into the Zambird, Zambull and Zambase; the Zambird can transform into the Zambo-Ace)
Have the Zambot 3, or have Kappei
notes: Meeting any one condition brings in all of that series' characters and units; nothing more joins if you already have a unit from that series

blocks.title: Link stage
notes: Each Link stage has a ground and a space version, chosen by whether the originally scheduled next stage is in space

blocks.title: How Link works in this port
items: Pick “Link” in the intermission menu to open the Link page: three series cards; check the series to add, then “Next: Link”
Card states: joined (grayed out, can't be selected again), scheduled (the next stage is already the link stage; the checkbox is locked), available
Then the original “GB Link” screen opens as usual; press B to return to the intermission menu
The matching link stage is inserted before the next battle, with the newly joining characters on your side; afterwards you return to the originally scheduled next stage
Link stage defeat condition: the game is over if a newly joined character is destroyed
The original link pulls the experience of pilots shared by both games up to the higher of the two; this port's virtual cartridge mirrors your own pilots directly, so nobody's level changes

blocks.title: Other
items: After a Link, some later stages have extra dialogue for these characters
Once Zambot 3 joins, it can use the combination attack “Space Combination Attack” with the Daitarn 3

After a Link, the title screen's Sound Test gains “F91ガンダム出撃”, “行けザンボット3” and “ゴーショーグン発進せよ”, and Karaoke gains two songs for the Zambot 3 and GoShogun; the condition is that these units have been on the team, not the Link itself {+}

A newly joined pilot's level = team average level + 1 (Cecily gets the average); the average is taken over the 15 highest-level pilots on the team who are assigned to units, rounded down, capped at 95 and at stages cleared + 40 {+}{?}
